newsitem.title: NORWAY: BALTICS-NORWAY INVITES U.S. TO TALK ON BALTIC SECURITY.
newsitem.headline: BALTICS-NORWAY INVITES U.S. TO TALK ON BALTIC SECURITY.

text.p: Norway said on Monday it has invited U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright to a meeting of Nordic and Baltic foreign ministers in September as it seeks to boost security in the Baltic region.
Foreign Ministry spokesman Ingvard Havnen said Norway saw the meeting as a chance to talk about NATO enlargement as well as the usual Nordic-Baltic cooperation issues.
"We have to find ways to try to integrate the Baltic states, whether it be on security policy or on a political or economic level," Havnen said.
"We see the need for integration not as something only of concern to the Nordic or Baltic countries but it is also important to our allies such as the United States," he added.
Latvia, Lithuania and Estonia are anxious to reinforce ties with the West after spending 50 years as unwilling members of the former Soviet Union.
All three have applied for NATO membership but diplomats say they are unlikely to enter the alliance in a first wave of enlargement due to strong Russian objections.
The Nordic countries -- Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway and Sweden -- have been the staunchest supporters of the Balts.
Nordic and Baltic diplomats have been involved in talks to find a security arrangement that would assuage Baltic fears of Russia and boost security if they do not gain entry to NATO.
